input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "ensures",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The postcondition of lemma equivalenceNoOrder contains a spurious conjunct '&& i != 0' inside the quantifier body (parsed as s[i]==s[j] && i != 0). For any non-empty s, the instance i=j=0 makes the right-hand side false, while allEqual(s) can be true (e.g. a constant sequence), so the equivalence is false and cannot be proved. Removing '&& i != 0' restores the intended statement that allEqual is equivalent to equality over ordered index pairs i<=j, which Dafny proves automatically."}
EOF
sed -i '10s/ \&\& i != 0//' program.dfy && sed -n 10p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
I fixed the postcondition and `program.dfy` now verifies: Dafny reports 17 verified, 0 errors.

**What was wrong:** the `ensures` clause of the lemma `equivalenceNoOrder` (line 10) had an extra `&& i != 0` at the end. Dafny read it as part of the quantifier body, so the right-hand side said `s[i]==s[j] && i != 0` for every pair of indices with `i <= j`. For any non-empty sequence, the pair `i = j = 0` makes that false. But `allEqual(s)` is true for, say, a sequence where every element is the same. So the "if and only if" was simply false and could never be proved.

**Fix:** I removed `&& i != 0`, so line 10 now reads:
```dafny
ensures allEqual(s) <==> forall i,j::0<=i<=j<|s| ==> s[i]==s[j]
```
This is the intended statement: all elements are equal exactly when every pair of indices with `i <= j` holds equal values. Dafny proves it with the existing empty body.

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before the edit, with `spec_element: "ensures"` and `proof_obligation: "bridge"`. This lemma has no loop, so none of the three categories fits exactly. I picked "bridge" because the failure is a postcondition that can't be shown to hold on return.
